title: How many bananas would it take to kill you with radiation?

lines.text: How many bananas would it take to kill you with radiation?
Bananas really are radioactive. Each one holds a pinch of potassium-40.
One banana gives you about a fiftieth of a dental X-ray.
A deadly dose? Roughly fifty million bananas.
So you start eating. A hundred a day.
But your body keeps potassium at one steady level. Your kidneys dump the extra within hours.
So the radiation never builds up. Not ever.
You survived. Comment what you want to know next.

experiment.note: Prototype for george (2026-11-25), not a daily episode: cel-shaded full 3D sets (kitchen, street) plus a clean blue studio, real camera moves, ink outlines.

facts.claim: One banana ~0.1 microsievert (banana equivalent dose), from potassium-40
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana_equivalent_dose ; University of Groningen radiation protection A-Z: https://www.rug.nl/education/courses/other-education/radiation-protection/a-z/a-z-data/banana-equivalent-dose

facts.claim: Dental X-ray ~5 microsieverts, so a banana is ~1/50
~5 Sv acute dose is roughly lethal (LD50/60 ~4-5 Gy) -> 5 Sv / 0.1 uSv = 50 million bananas
The dose does not accumulate: potassium is held at a constant level and excess is excreted by the kidneys
